money_at_stake.basis: Re-verified this occurrence directly against the Federal Reserve's own transcript (re-fetched this run, federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/warsh20260828a.htm, 2026-08-28): Chairman Warsh reaffirmed the 2 percent PCE target as 'a firm, fixed target,' said the summer's better-than-expected PCE and CPI readings do not show underlying trends have meaningfully improved, declined to give forward guidance ('the role of forward guidance should be limited and circumscribed'), and declined a mechanical policy rule. A monetary-policy stance speech has no discrete annual spend, capex, or revenue pool of its own the way a build program, subsidy, or procurement award does: it changes the price applied to money and assets already committed, it does not commit new capital itself. The transcript states no dollar figure that could seed this leg. The only candidate discrete pool found is the outstanding US Treasury market ($31.5 trillion as of July 2026, +8.6% Y/Y, SIFMA, re-fetched and quoted this run), and using that aggregate market size as 'the pool this occurrence moves' would misattribute the pre-existing size of a market that discounts continuously to one speech and one resulting yield move, which is exactly the reasoned-but-unsourced number method section 0.2 forbids. This run also re-fetched the two market-reaction sources (CNBC's yield-move article, a Bloomberg live blog) the prior version cited for same-day repricing figures (2-year yield, index moves, rate-hike odds); both returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and archive.org's availability API returned no snapshot for either URL, so those items are deleted under the source_excerpt discipline rather than repaired with a substitute source. The leg's conclusion no longer rests on those figures at all: it rests solely on the two sources actually reopened and quoted this run (the transcript and SIFMA), both of which support the same finding that no discrete pool is citable. No band assigned. This remains Nell's control case: maximum apparent money, near-zero unmappedness, and on inspection no citable discrete pool at all.

evidence.claim: Chairman Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote: the Fed's 2 percent PCE price-stability objective 'is a firm, fixed target'; the summer's better-than-expected PCE and CPI readings 'do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved'; on forward guidance, 'In normal times, the role of forward guidance should be limited and circumscribed. Otherwise it risks creating ambiguity in the name of clarity'; on a mechanical policy rule, 'I wish our understanding of the economy were so precise as to provide a mechanical, tried-and-true answer.' None of these statements names a dollar figure, spend program, or revenue pool.
evidence.source_name: Federal Reserve Board, Keynote remarks by Chairman Warsh at the 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium
source_excerpt: The Fed's price-stability objective of 2 percent, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, is a firm, fixed target.
And while this summer's PCE and CPI readings were better than expected, they do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved.
In normal times, the role of forward guidance should be limited and circumscribed. Otherwise it risks creating ambiguity in the name of clarity.
I wish our understanding of the economy were so precise as to provide a mechanical, tried-and-true answer—that some simple function like a Taylor rule could be rigorously relied upon.

evidence.claim: SIFMA's Treasury statistics page, under 'YTD 2026 statistics include': outstanding US Treasury securities were 'Outstanding (as of July) $31.5 trillion, +8.6% Y/Y.' Cited only to show why using aggregate market size as a stand-in for 'money at stake' would be the reasoned-but-unsourced number this leg forbids, not used to set a band.
